objective: Ship three focused pre-V4 releases (Memory Clarity, Planning Workflow, Agent Visibility) so Crowley is trustworthy before V4 connectivity.
context: Baseline: V3.9.1 Repository & CI is live with git, Actions CI, memory trail, tickets, and multi-agent sync. Guiding principle: natural in conversation, auditable on demand. Full ticket slices also live in tickets/pre_v4_release_plan.json.
decisions: Pre-V4 work is a memory-led three-release ladder: V3.9.2 → V3.9.3 → V3.9.4
Draft tickets #4-#8 are cancelled as superseded; active implementation tickets are #9-#23
V4 connectivity waits until canon, retrieval inspection, planning packets, agent visibility, and test isolation are in place
Crowley remains the only hub — no direct Codex-to-Cursor messaging
non_goals: V4 external collectors or multi-project commands in this initiative
One giant Cursor prompt for all pre-V4 work
risks: project_state may lag filesystem docs until lock-in
Legacy tasks and open_loops coexist with tickets — tickets are the agent board
Planning packets minted before approval could send Cursor down stale paths
qa_expectations: Unit tests for new workflow surfaces; UI smoke on Memory/Tickets/Agent Feed; python -m unittest discover -s tests -q; manual Codex/Cursor sync + ticket close with handoff.
next_action: After Mr. Go approves, Codex runs: ./venv/bin/python3 scripts/codex_sync.py --create-tickets tickets/pre_v4_release_plan.json

approval.note: Pre-V4 release plan approved as durable planning artifact. Example only — tickets already minted as #9-#23.

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: document planning roles and Cursor-ready tickets
tickets.description: Create docs/V3.9.3_PLANNING_WORKFLOW.md explaining how Mr. Go, Codex, Cursor, and Crowley collaborate.
acceptance: Doc explains roles: Mr. Go sets intent, Codex plans, Cursor builds, Crowley stores truth
Doc explains when to brainstorm versus when to mint tickets
Doc defines Cursor-ready tickets with scope, acceptance criteria, QA expectation, and non-goals
WHERE_WE_ARE links to the workflow doc in the agent ritual section
No wording implies direct Codex-to-Cursor messaging

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: add planning packet template
tickets.description: Add reusable planning packet JSON template and Pre-V4 example before ticket minting.
acceptance: Template includes objective, context, decisions, non-goals, risks, ticket slices, acceptance criteria, QA expectations, and next action
Template can be copied into a ticket JSON packet without losing core fields
Example packet uses the Pre-V4 release plan as a realistic reference
Docs explain that planning packet approval happens before Cursor implementation

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: add Agent Feed tab
tickets.description: Add Intelligence drawer Agent Feed tab from existing agent activity APIs.
acceptance: Intelligence drawer includes an Agent Feed tab
Tab renders recent agent events newest-first with source, timestamp, and summary
Uses existing read APIs or dashboard snapshot
No direct agent-to-agent channel is introduced
